import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.26

by G. S. Makanin

b) Does there exist an algorithm which decides whether the equation of the form
$w(x_{i_1}^{\varphi_1}, \ldots, x_{i_n}^{\varphi_n}) = 1$ is soluble in a free group
where $\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_n$ are automorphisms of this group?

Here $x^{\varphi}$ denotes the image of $x$ under $\varphi$, the $x_i$ are unknowns (the same
unknown may occur several times, under different automorphisms) and $w$ is a group word in
$n$ letters and in constants of the free group. Part b) is the only part of the problem listed
in the cited edition of the notebook.

## Formalisation

The free group is $F = F_r$ of finite rank $r$ with basis $a_0, \ldots, a_{r-1}$, modelled as
`FreeGroup (Fin r)`. The source does not say whether the rank is fixed or part of the input; we
fix it, and ask for an algorithm for every rank $r$.

The word $w$ is allowed to contain constants from $F$ (as in Makanin's setting of equations in
free groups). The source does not say so explicitly, but without constants every such equation
has the trivial solution $x_1 = \dots = x_m = 1$ (see `TwistedWord.isSoluble_of_forall_isRight`)
and the question would be vacuous.

The left-hand side $w(x_{i_1}^{\varphi_1}, \ldots, x_{i_n}^{\varphi_n})$ is entered as a word
(`TwistedWord`) whose letters, each with an exponent $\pm 1$, are basis elements $a_k$ of $F$
and twisted unknowns $x_i^{\varphi}$. This is the same as giving $w$ as a word in $n$ symbols
together with the data $i_1, \ldots, i_n$ and $\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_n$. An automorphism
$\varphi$ is specified by the images $\varphi(a_0), \ldots, \varphi(a_{r-1})$ of the basis, given
as words (`BasisImages`). Such data always determine an endomorphism of $F$, so the requirement
that the $\varphi_j$ be automorphisms is a promise on the input: the algorithm must answer
correctly on every input all of whose twists are automorphisms. "Algorithm" is `Computable`,
Mathlib's notion of a computable function between `Primcodable` types.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«10.26»
variable {r : ℕ}

blocks.code: abbrev BasisImages (r : ℕ) := Fin r → List (Fin r × Bool)
blocks.docstring:
Data specifying an endomorphism of the free group `FreeGroup (Fin r)` with basis
`a_0, …, a_{r-1}`: the image of each `a_k` is given as a word, i.e. a list of letters
`a_l^{±1}`, where `(l, true)` stands for `a_l` and `(l, false)` for `a_l⁻¹`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin r)) / FreeGroup (Fin r) ≃* FreeGroup (Fin r) (not encodable as algorithm input); FreeGroup.lift (used to interpret the data).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».BasisImages
justification.why_needed: Finite, Primcodable input specifying an endomorphism/automorphism of `FreeGroup (Fin r)` by the images of the basis elements as words; `MulAut (FreeGroup (Fin r))` is not Primcodable.

blocks.name: BasisImages
blocks.text:
/-- Data specifying an endomorphism of the free group `FreeGroup (Fin r)` with basis
`a_0, …, a_{r-1}`: the image of each `a_k` is given as a word, i.e. a list of letters
`a_l^{±1}`, where `(l, true)` stands for `a_l` and `(l, false)` for `a_l⁻¹`. -/
abbrev BasisImages (r : ℕ) := Fin r → List (Fin r × Bool)

blocks.code:
def BasisImages.toHom (f : BasisImages r) : FreeGroup (Fin r) →* FreeGroup (Fin r) :=
  FreeGroup.lift fun k => FreeGroup.mk (f k)
blocks.docstring:
The endomorphism of `FreeGroup (Fin r)` sending each basis element `a_k` to the word
`f k`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».BasisImages.toHom
justification.why_needed: The endomorphism `FreeGroup.lift (fun k => FreeGroup.mk (f k))` determined by basis images.

blocks.name: BasisImages.toHom
blocks.text:
/-- The endomorphism of `FreeGroup (Fin r)` sending each basis element `a_k` to the word
`f k`. -/
def BasisImages.toHom (f : BasisImages r) : FreeGroup (Fin r) →* FreeGroup (Fin r) :=
  FreeGroup.lift fun k => FreeGroup.mk (f k)

blocks.code:
def BasisImages.IsAut (f : BasisImages r) : Prop :=
  Function.Bijective f.toHom
blocks.docstring: The basis images `f` specify an automorphism of `FreeGroup (Fin r)`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».BasisImages.IsAut
justification.why_needed: The promise that the twist data specify an automorphism (`Function.Bijective f.toHom`).

blocks.name: BasisImages.IsAut

blocks.code: def BasisImages.identity (r : ℕ) : BasisImages r := fun k => [(k, true)]
blocks.docstring: The basis images of the identity automorphism.

justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».BasisImages.identity
justification.why_needed: Basis images of the identity automorphism, used only in the test lemmas.

blocks.name: BasisImages.identity
blocks.text:
/-- The basis images of the identity automorphism. -/
def BasisImages.identity (r : ℕ) : BasisImages r := fun k => [(k, true)]

blocks.code: abbrev Letter (r : ℕ) := Fin r ⊕ (ℕ × BasisImages r)
blocks.docstring:
A letter of a twisted word over `FreeGroup (Fin r)`: either a constant, namely a basis
element `a_k` (`Sum.inl k`), or a twisted unknown `x_i^φ` (`Sum.inr (i, φ)`), where the
unknowns are `x_i` for `i : ℕ` and `φ` is given by its basis images.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Plain Sum type (it is an abbrev of one).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».Letter
justification.why_needed: Alphabet of a twisted word: `Fin r ⊕ (ℕ × BasisImages r)` (constant basis element or twisted unknown x_i^φ).

blocks.name: Letter
blocks.text:
/-- A letter of a twisted word over `FreeGroup (Fin r)`: either a constant, namely a basis
element `a_k` (`Sum.inl k`), or a twisted unknown `x_i^φ` (`Sum.inr (i, φ)`), where the
unknowns are `x_i` for `i : ℕ` and `φ` is given by its basis images. -/
abbrev Letter (r : ℕ) := Fin r ⊕ (ℕ × BasisImages r)

blocks.code: abbrev TwistedWord (r : ℕ) := List (Letter r × Bool)
blocks.docstring:
A twisted word over `FreeGroup (Fin r)`, i.e. the left-hand side
`w(x_{i_1}^{φ_1}, …, x_{i_n}^{φ_n})` of a twisted equation `w(…) = 1`, written as a list of
letters with exponents `±1` (`true` for `+1`, `false` for `-1`).

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup (Fin n ⊕ Fin r) with a dependent slot assignment (no Primcodable for FreeGroup or Sigma types in Mathlib).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».TwistedWord
justification.why_needed: The input of the algorithm: `List (Letter r × Bool)`, the left-hand side w(x_{i_1}^{φ_1},…,x_{i_n}^{φ_n}) as a list of signed letters; Primcodable via Mathlib's List/Prod/Sum/Fin/finArrow instances. `FreeGroup (Letter r)` has no Primcodable instance.

blocks.name: TwistedWord
blocks.text:
/-- A twisted word over `FreeGroup (Fin r)`, i.e. the left-hand side
`w(x_{i_1}^{φ_1}, …, x_{i_n}^{φ_n})` of a twisted equation `w(…) = 1`, written as a list of
letters with exponents `±1` (`true` for `+1`, `false` for `-1`). -/
abbrev TwistedWord (r : ℕ) := List (Letter r × Bool)

blocks.code:
def TwistedWord.eval (w : TwistedWord r) (x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r)) : FreeGroup (Fin r) :=
  FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim FreeGroup.of fun p => p.2.toHom (x p.1)) (FreeGroup.mk w)
blocks.docstring:
The value of the twisted word `w` when the unknowns take the values `x i`: each constant
`a_k` is evaluated to itself and each twisted unknown `x_i^φ` to `φ (x i)`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».TwistedWord.eval
justification.why_needed: Value of the twisted word at an assignment x : ℕ → F, via `FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim FreeGroup.of fun p => p.2.toHom (x p.1)) (FreeGroup.mk w)`.

blocks.name: TwistedWord.eval
blocks.text:
/-- The value of the twisted word `w` when the unknowns take the values `x i`: each constant
`a_k` is evaluated to itself and each twisted unknown `x_i^φ` to `φ (x i)`. -/
def TwistedWord.eval (w : TwistedWord r) (x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r)) : FreeGroup (Fin r) :=
  FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim FreeGroup.of fun p => p.2.toHom (x p.1)) (FreeGroup.mk w)

blocks.code:
def TwistedWord.IsSoluble (w : TwistedWord r) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r), w.eval x = 1
blocks.docstring:
The twisted equation `w = 1` is soluble in `FreeGroup (Fin r)`: some assignment of the
unknowns makes its left-hand side equal to `1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib (no notion of equations in groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».TwistedWord.IsSoluble
justification.why_needed: Solubility of the twisted equation w = 1 in F: `∃ x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r), w.eval x = 1`.

blocks.name: TwistedWord.IsSoluble
blocks.text:
/-- The twisted equation `w = 1` is soluble in `FreeGroup (Fin r)`: some assignment of the
unknowns makes its left-hand side equal to `1`. -/
def TwistedWord.IsSoluble (w : TwistedWord r) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r), w.eval x = 1

blocks.code:
def TwistedWord.IsAutTwisted (w : TwistedWord r) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : ℕ) (φ : BasisImages r) (b : Bool), (Sum.inr (i, φ), b) ∈ w → φ.IsAut
blocks.docstring:
All twists `φ` occurring in the twisted word `w` are automorphisms of `FreeGroup (Fin r)`
(and not merely endomorphisms).

justification.name: Kourovka.«10.26».TwistedWord.IsAutTwisted
justification.why_needed: The promise 'φ_1,…,φ_n are automorphisms': every twist occurring in w satisfies `IsAut`.

blocks.name: TwistedWord.IsAutTwisted
blocks.text:
/-- All twists `φ` occurring in the twisted word `w` are automorphisms of `FreeGroup (Fin r)`
(and not merely endomorphisms). -/
def TwistedWord.IsAutTwisted (w : TwistedWord r) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : ℕ) (φ : BasisImages r) (b : Bool), (Sum.inr (i, φ), b) ∈ w → φ.IsAut

    ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ alg : TwistedWord r → Bool, Computable alg ∧

blocks.docstring:
b) Does there exist an algorithm which decides whether the equation of the form
$w(x_{i_1}^{\varphi_1}, \ldots, x_{i_n}^{\varphi_n}) = 1$ is soluble in a free group
where $\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_n$ are automorphisms of this group?

Formally: for every finite rank $r$, is there a computable function `TwistedWord r → Bool`
which, on every twisted word all of whose twists are automorphisms of $F_r$, returns `true`

the automorphisms are given by the images of a free basis, and the word may contain constants

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem TwistedWord.isSoluble_of_forall_isRight (w : TwistedWord r)
    (hw : ∀ l ∈ w, l.1.isRight) : w.IsSoluble := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => 1, ?_⟩
  rw [TwistedWord.eval, FreeGroup.lift_mk]
  refine List.prod_eq_one fun y hy => ?_
  obtain ⟨⟨l, b⟩, hl, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hy
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := Sum.isRight_iff.mp (hw _ hl)
  simp only at hp
  subst hp
  cases b <;> simp
blocks.docstring:
A twisted equation without constants is always soluble, by the trivial solution
$x_i = 1$.
blocks.name: TwistedWord.isSoluble_of_forall_isRight
blocks.text:
/-- A twisted equation without constants is always soluble, by the trivial solution
$x_i = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem TwistedWord.isSoluble_of_forall_isRight (w : TwistedWord r)
    (hw : ∀ l ∈ w, l.1.isRight) : w.IsSoluble := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => 1, ?_⟩
  rw [TwistedWord.eval, FreeGroup.lift_mk]
  refine List.prod_eq_one fun y hy => ?_
  obtain ⟨⟨l, b⟩, hl, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hy
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := Sum.isRight_iff.mp (hw _ hl)
  simp only at hp
  subst hp
  cases b <;> simp

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isSoluble_example :
    TwistedWord.IsSoluble
      ([(Sum.inr (0, BasisImages.identity 1), true), (Sum.inl 0, false)] : TwistedWord 1) :=
  ⟨fun _ => FreeGroup.of 0, by
    simp [TwistedWord.eval, BasisImages.toHom, BasisImages.identity]
    exact mul_inv_cancel _⟩
blocks.docstring: The (untwisted) equation `x_0 a_0⁻¹ = 1` is soluble in the free group of rank `1`.
blocks.name: isSoluble_example
blocks.text:

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isSoluble_example :
    TwistedWord.IsSoluble
      ([(Sum.inr (0, BasisImages.identity 1), true), (Sum.inl 0, false)] : TwistedWord 1) :=
  ⟨fun _ => FreeGroup.of 0, by
    simp [TwistedWord.eval, BasisImages.toHom, BasisImages.identity]
    exact mul_inv_cancel _⟩

theorem not_isSoluble_example :
    ¬ TwistedWord.IsSoluble ([(Sum.inl 0, true)] : TwistedWord 1) := by
  rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
  simp [TwistedWord.eval] at hx
blocks.docstring: The equation `a_0 = 1` (with no unknowns) is not soluble in the free group of rank `1`.

end Kourovka.«10.26»

claims.decomposer_note: Single open yes/no decidability question (sole remaining lettered part b), no \zva star): the Prop is the existence of an algorithm (to be expressed via computability, e.g. a computable/decidable predicate on an encoded input) which, given a finite-rank free group F, a word w (in variables and, as in Makanin's setting, possibly constants from F), the index assignment i_1..i_n (the same variable x_i may occur several times under different twists) and automorphisms φ_1..φ_n of F (each specified by the images of a free basis), decides whether there exist x_1,…,x_m ∈ F with w(φ_1(x_{i_1}),…,φ_n(x_{i_n})) = 1; the exponent notation x^φ means the image of x under φ; whether the rank of F is fixed or part of the input, and whether w may contain constants, are left implicit by the source and should be recorded in the docstring.
claims.reviewer_why: c01's design (shared with c02/c07/c08) is a faithful promise-problem formalization: for each finite rank r, a `Computable` function on the Primcodable type of twisted words over `FreeGroup (Fin r)` (letters = basis constants a_k or twisted unknowns x_i^φ with φ given by basis images, each with sign), correct on every input whose twists are bijective endomorphisms, returning true iff ∃ x : ℕ → F_r with w(φ_j(x_{i_j})) = 1. Sign convention verified against `FreeGroup.lift_mk`; parse of `→ (… ↔ …)` verified via #print. c01 chosen for the clearest module/theorem docstrings recording the implicit choices (rank fixed, constants allowed); I added c08's API lemma that constant-free equations are trivially soluble (documents why constants must be allowed) and a `toHom_identity` lemma. c02/c08 are equivalent alternatives; c07 lacks tests. c03/c04/c05 (rank as input) are also faithful readings but more cumbersome and the fixed-rank reading matches the source's 'a free group … automorphisms of this group' and the repo precedent (BranchingVAS: `∀ {d}, ComputablePred …`). c06 is REJECTED: its statement `code.IsValid → (…) ↔ code.IsSolvable` parses as `(IsValid → alg = true) ↔ IsSolvable` (→ binds tighter than ↔), forcing every invalid code to be solvable, so its right-hand side is provably false.

namespace Kourovka.«10.26»

variable {r : ℕ}

/-- Data specifying an endomorphism of the free group `FreeGroup (Fin r)` with basis
`a_0, …, a_{r-1}`: the image of each `a_k` is given as a word, i.e. a list of letters
`a_l^{±1}`, where `(l, true)` stands for `a_l` and `(l, false)` for `a_l⁻¹`. -/
abbrev BasisImages (r : ℕ) := Fin r → List (Fin r × Bool)

/-- The endomorphism of `FreeGroup (Fin r)` sending each basis element `a_k` to the word
`f k`. -/
def BasisImages.toHom (f : BasisImages r) : FreeGroup (Fin r) →* FreeGroup (Fin r) :=
  FreeGroup.lift fun k => FreeGroup.mk (f k)

/-- The basis images `f` specify an automorphism of `FreeGroup (Fin r)`. -/
def BasisImages.IsAut (f : BasisImages r) : Prop :=
  Function.Bijective f.toHom

/-- The basis images of the identity automorphism. -/
def BasisImages.identity (r : ℕ) : BasisImages r := fun k => [(k, true)]

/-- A letter of a twisted word over `FreeGroup (Fin r)`: either a constant, namely a basis
element `a_k` (`Sum.inl k`), or a twisted unknown `x_i^φ` (`Sum.inr (i, φ)`), where the
unknowns are `x_i` for `i : ℕ` and `φ` is given by its basis images. -/
abbrev Letter (r : ℕ) := Fin r ⊕ (ℕ × BasisImages r)

/-- A twisted word over `FreeGroup (Fin r)`, i.e. the left-hand side
`w(x_{i_1}^{φ_1}, …, x_{i_n}^{φ_n})` of a twisted equation `w(…) = 1`, written as a list of
letters with exponents `±1` (`true` for `+1`, `false` for `-1`). -/
abbrev TwistedWord (r : ℕ) := List (Letter r × Bool)

/-- The value of the twisted word `w` when the unknowns take the values `x i`: each constant
`a_k` is evaluated to itself and each twisted unknown `x_i^φ` to `φ (x i)`. -/
def TwistedWord.eval (w : TwistedWord r) (x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r)) : FreeGroup (Fin r) :=
  FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim FreeGroup.of fun p => p.2.toHom (x p.1)) (FreeGroup.mk w)

/-- The twisted equation `w = 1` is soluble in `FreeGroup (Fin r)`: some assignment of the
unknowns makes its left-hand side equal to `1`. -/
def TwistedWord.IsSoluble (w : TwistedWord r) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin r), w.eval x = 1

/-- All twists `φ` occurring in the twisted word `w` are automorphisms of `FreeGroup (Fin r)`
(and not merely endomorphisms). -/
def TwistedWord.IsAutTwisted (w : TwistedWord r) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : ℕ) (φ : BasisImages r) (b : Bool), (Sum.inr (i, φ), b) ∈ w → φ.IsAut

/--
b) Does there exist an algorithm which decides whether the equation of the form
$w(x_{i_1}^{\varphi_1}, \ldots, x_{i_n}^{\varphi_n}) = 1$ is soluble in a free group
where $\varphi_1, \ldots, \varphi_n$ are automorphisms of this group?

Formally: for every finite rank $r$, is there a computable function `TwistedWord r → Bool`
which, on every twisted word all of whose twists are automorphisms of $F_r$, returns `true`
exactly when the equation is soluble in $F_r$? The rank $r$ is fixed (not part of the input),
the automorphisms are given by the images of a free basis, and the word may contain constants
from $F_r$; see the module docstring.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.26».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ alg : TwistedWord r → Bool, Computable alg ∧
      ∀ w : TwistedWord r, w.IsAutTwisted → (alg w = true ↔ w.IsSoluble) := by
  sorry

/-- The identity basis images specify the identity endomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem BasisImages.toHom_identity : (BasisImages.identity r).toHom = MonoidHom.id _ :=
  FreeGroup.lift_of_eq_id _

/-- The identity basis images specify an automorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem BasisImages.isAut_identity : (BasisImages.identity r).IsAut := by
  rw [IsAut, BasisImages.toHom_identity]
  exact Function.bijective_id

/-- A twisted equation without constants is always soluble, by the trivial solution
$x_i = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem TwistedWord.isSoluble_of_forall_isRight (w : TwistedWord r)
    (hw : ∀ l ∈ w, l.1.isRight) : w.IsSoluble := by
  refine ⟨fun _ => 1, ?_⟩
  rw [TwistedWord.eval, FreeGroup.lift_mk]
  refine List.prod_eq_one fun y hy => ?_
  obtain ⟨⟨l, b⟩, hl, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hy
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := Sum.isRight_iff.mp (hw _ hl)
  simp only at hp
  subst hp
  cases b <;> simp

/-- The (untwisted) equation `x_0 a_0⁻¹ = 1` is soluble in the free group of rank `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isSoluble_example :
    TwistedWord.IsSoluble
      ([(Sum.inr (0, BasisImages.identity 1), true), (Sum.inl 0, false)] : TwistedWord 1) :=
  ⟨fun _ => FreeGroup.of 0, by
    simp [TwistedWord.eval, BasisImages.toHom, BasisImages.identity]
    exact mul_inv_cancel _⟩

/-- The equation `a_0 = 1` (with no unknowns) is not soluble in the free group of rank `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem not_isSoluble_example :
    ¬ TwistedWord.IsSoluble ([(Sum.inl 0, true)] : TwistedWord 1) := by
  rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
  simp [TwistedWord.eval] at hx

end Kourovka.«10.26»

items: Rank of the free group is FIXED (quantified outside: `∀ r, ∃ alg …`), i.e. the question asks for an algorithm for each finite rank r; the rank is not part of the input. The source leaves this implicit; recorded in the module and theorem docstrings. A positive answer to the uniform version implies this one, and a negative answer for any fixed rank refutes both.

The word w may contain constants (coefficients) from F, encoded as signed basis letters a_k^{±1} (every element of F is such a product). Justification: without constants x_i = 1 is always a solution and the question would be vacuous; this is also Makanin's standard setting. Recorded in the docstrings.

The equation w(x_{i_1}^{φ_1},…,x_{i_n}^{φ_n}) = 1 is entered directly as the substituted word: a list of signed letters, each a constant a_k or a twisted unknown x_i^φ (`Sum.inr (i, φ)`). This is exactly the class of equations obtained from a word w(y_1,…,y_n) with constants plus an index assignment i_j and twists φ_j by substituting y_j ↦ x_{i_j}^{φ_j} (and conversely, each occurrence is a slot). It avoids dependent input types (Mathlib has no `Primcodable` for Sigma types or for `FreeGroup`). Unknowns are indexed by ℕ rather than Fin m (only finitely many occur).

Automorphisms are specified by the images of the free basis (as words), per the decomposition notes. Such data always give an endomorphism (`BasisImages.toHom = FreeGroup.lift`), so 'the φ_j are automorphisms' (`Function.Bijective`) is imposed as a promise: `∃ alg, Computable alg ∧ ∀ w, w.IsAutTwisted → (alg w = true ↔ w.IsSoluble)`, instead of `ComputablePred` on a subtype (which would require a `PrimrecPred` proof of automorphism-checking). `ComputablePred p ↔ ∃ f, Computable f ∧ p = (f · = true)` in Mathlib, so this is the standard promise-problem generalization.

A twisted-unknown letter with exponent −1 evaluates to (φ(x_i))⁻¹ = φ(x_i⁻¹); `FreeGroup.mk` identifies words up to free reduction on the letter alphabet, which is consistent with evaluation since evaluation is a group homomorphism.

Three `@[category test]` lemmas are included: identity basis images are an automorphism (so the promise is satisfiable), the untwisted equation x_0 a_0⁻¹ = 1 is soluble, and a_0 = 1 is not soluble (so solubility is not trivial).

reviewer_notes: Source ambiguities (recorded in the module docstring): (1) whether the rank of the free group is fixed or part of the algorithm's input — the final file fixes the rank and asks for an algorithm for every finite rank r (`∀ r, ∃ alg`), the more literal reading of 'in a free group … automorphisms of this group' and consistent with the repo's BranchingVAS idiom; the uniform-in-r version (c03/c04/c05) is stronger in principle but would be expected to have the same answer. (2) Whether w may contain constants — constants are allowed (Makanin's setting); without them x_i = 1 always solves the equation (proved as API lemma `TwistedWord.isSoluble_of_forall_isRight`). (3) Automorphism requirement is a promise on the input (algorithm must be correct on inputs whose basis-image data define bijective endomorphisms); since 'basis images define an automorphism' is decidable, this is equivalent to a ComputablePred on the restricted instance set, but the promise form avoids needing a Primcodable subtype. Infinite-rank free groups are excluded since automorphisms could not then be finitely specified. Candidate omissions: none — all 8 formalized the slot; c06 was rejected for the precedence bug described in per_slot. Sandbox note: `lakefile.toml` modification and `run/` directory in the checkout pre-existed and were not made by me.
